assertion_analysis.failure_condition: test_solver_loads_the_certified_carrier reddens if certified_machine is absent or renamed (the base arm fails by ImportError at baseline_suite) and if the certified 550 rung resolves to a machine other than 553 cells; it is a real guard on the new route, though its base failure observes the introduced symbol's absence rather than the axis read.

The assertion at line 73 reddens if the signed Hessian stops being negative definite; the block at lines 78-79 builds TopologyConvention.from_cocos(17,-1.0) and requires valid=false with a NaN axis, so it fires on the polarity gate rather than restating a passed-in value, and is an independent negative control.

np.testing.assert_allclose(reading.axis, expected_axis, atol=1e-12) compares the read's returned axis against the same array the test supplied at roots.position; with a single root the read returns that value whenever it is not refused, so this assertion cannot redden for any ranking regression that line 75 does not already catch and is a duplicate of the input, not an independent measurement.

test_solver_job_arguments_match_parser parses the actual deep-job.sh and two_merit_job.sh command lines through solver.main() and reddens with SystemExit when the command passes the removed --cache; solver_cli_negative.log shows FF on the pre-repair commands, so this guard is verified by reinstating the regression rather than by observing a passing run.

findings.text: follow-on: the suite paragraph reports the fast-map arm as '14 passed and one failed' and the head as 'all 15 + 2 + 22', but the gate log solver_cli_baseline.log shows 16 passed and 1 failed for the fast-map arm (and 17 passed at the head), and both the same fragment's later paragraph (line 10, '17 fast-map ... 16 + 2 + 22') and the research record (docs/research/carrier-axis-orientation.html:48, '16 passed, 1 failed') give the current counts. The 14/15 figures are stale from before the two parser-test cases landed; a landing record that contradicts its own sibling paragraph and the log it cites misinforms the reader who opens the fragment.

follow-on: assert_allclose(reading.axis, expected_axis, atol=1e-12) compares the read's returned axis against the same array the test placed at roots.position, so with a single root the assertion holds for any accepted root and cannot redden for a ranking regression that the valid/qualified assertion at line 75 does not already catch; the axis acceptance durability rests on line 75, not on line 76.

follow-on: certified_machine re-derives the fixture identity with fixture.cache_identity(carrier, requested_cells=requested, wall_nodes=WALL_POINT_COUNT, wall=wall) instead of asking the owner whether the object is published, while the owner scripts/prototypes/support/certificate_fixtures.py:232 -> scripts/analytic_oracle_fixtures/measure.py:cached_machine builds the identity with an added builder=resolve_builder(builder). The pre-check omits that builder argument, so a later change to the owner's identity recipe would desync the guard from the digest cached_carrier actually requests; it is a duplicated recipe, not a fork of the loader, and the guard is otherwise a correct fail-before-cold-build wrapper.

follow-on: cold-job.sh:28-33 passes --cache both to its cold.py wrapper, which delegates to the fast_map_production solver parser, and directly to the solver, which no longer defines --cache; those two cold-job.sh lines are the one path into a production caller that would break, not the two the node fixed. Each command now exits 2 at argparse before the solve. The node was fenced out of scripts/prototypes/fine_grid_convergence and names this in the manifest follow_ons, so it is out of scope for this verdict and blocks nothing; it is recorded because the landed removal makes it reachable.
